To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

meditation related neurobiological plasticity is associated to a functional and structural reorganization of brain areas involved in the control of attention and awareness, in a style dependent fashion.

meditation related neurophysiology is characterized by a complex pattern of activity in prefrontal and insula areas, and that this pattern is differentially modulated depending on the attentional state of the subject, and on whether the subject is a novice or an expert meditator.
FA and OM meditations are associated with different brain activity patterns in pre frontal, parietal and cingulate cortices, and in the insular cortex.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the neural correlates of focused attention, cognitive monitoring and emotion regulation in meditation, as well as their functional reorganization with practice.

the study of the neural correlates of the cognitive and emotional processes underlying meditation, with the goal of understanding the neurobiological mechanisms involved in the regulation of attention and awareness, and their relationship with the development of meditation expertise.
the study of meditation states as a complex form of self directed attention, and with the study of the neurophysiological correlates of attentional, cognitive and affective processes in meditation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the neural basis of focused attention and of cognitive monitoring in meditation is a massive self regulation of prefrontal cortex, anterior cingulate cortex and insular areas, which are the neural correlates of the attention setting and cognitive monitoring in the two main meditation styles.

meditation is not associated with a general deactivation, but with a massive self regulation, of brain areas associated to executive functions, attention and awareness processes, which is a key feature of the meditative state.

meditation practice induces a functional reorganization in the brain activity pattern for attentional and cognitive monitoring processes, which is related to a functional reorganisation of activity in prefrontal and insular brain areas.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

FA and OM meditation practices are characterized by a complex interplay between the anterior cingulate cortex and the dorsolateral pre frontal cortex, and that this interplay is modulated by the left insula.

meditation related neurophysiological plasticity is associated to a massive self regulation of attention, thought, and emotion processes, by a reorganization of the functional activity patterns in pre frontal cortex and insula.
meditation is a form of self directed neuroplasticity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
meditation related brain reorganization of activity is associated to the development of a more efficient executive control of attention and cognitive monitoring.

meditation is associated to the development of a self regulation mechanism of cognitive monitoring and attentional control, that is, a mechanism that allows the control of the engagement in conscious processing.
meditators are able to control their cognitive engagement in conscious sensory related, thought or emotional processing by massive self-regulation of fronto-parietal and insula regions.
